← DUNE II

BROWSER RECONSTRUCTION · VERSION 0.5 · ORIGINAL ART UPSCALED

The original artwork, upscaled.

This version compiles the recovered OpenDUNE C engine to WebAssembly. The original PAK files supply graphics, scenarios, EMC scripts, voices and music. The supplied DOS executable provides static evidence and bounded DOSBox-X comparisons; the browser runs the rebuilt C engine.

Original artwork upscaling

The default 1280×800 presentation applies the xBR pixel-art filter to the complete original game image. Terrain, buildings, units, fog, text, menus and cutscenes retain their original artwork and native compositing. No generated material textures or generated cover are used. Graphics lets you switch instantly to the unfiltered 1992 output.

xBR smooths nearby colour edges rather than inventing detail. If WebGL is unavailable, the browser uses indexed Scale2x. Native gameplay, input, saves, audio and timing are unchanged. The source download includes the upscaler, original and adapted shader, MIT license and provenance.

What changed

  • The native engine now drives terrain, combat, routing, special weapons, harvesting, production and campaign progression.
  • UNIT, BUILD and TEAM scripts dispatch their complete native callback tables. All 79 slots used by the supplied scripts have original function evidence.
  • All ten intro, interlude and House ending sequences use the native WSA, palette, subtitle, voice and timing paths. Narration queues and VOC silence blocks were restored from the supplied data.
  • The supplied ADL scores play through a Westwood driver at 72 Hz and Nuked OPL emulation. Music and sound effects share the original driver channels.
  • Native saves persist in browser storage and can be exported or imported. Browser backgrounding pauses the emulated clock and audio.

DOS comparison fixes

The comparison corrected byte-facing checks, aircraft firing while turning, structure-edge range, movement rounding and deviation control. Cutscene sound-effect attenuation now matches original OPL writes. Continuation-animation loading and INI parsing also received bounds fixes after sanitized scene tests.

Validation and limits

Terrain was compared against an independent C oracle for 48 mission seeds and three diagnostic seeds. Terrain-only MAP projections cover all 66 supplied scenarios. Combat arithmetic has more than 380,000 checked vectors. All 223 supplied VOC resources were decoded and compared, and all 37 nonzero music mappings were rendered; three mappings contain absent ADL entries and remain silent.

This is a source reconstruction with selected V1.07 compatibility patches, not a claim of instruction-for-instruction recovery. Real DOS allocator snapshots agree for the three tested terrain seeds; other adjacent-memory states remain outside that coverage. The archive lacks OK.VOC. Every campaign branch and finale has not been acceptance tested in the browser. Authorized DOSBox-X runs now cover three terrain seeds, 5,854 controlled combat cases, the introduction, all three endings, music-register traces and save cross-loading. Physical sound-card equivalence remains untested. The selected music reference is AdLib/OPL, rather than Roland MT-32 hardware.

Credits and source

Dune II and its original assets are by Westwood Studios and the original publishers and contributors. Their rights remain separate from the engine licenses. This is an independent reconstruction.

  • OpenDUNE contributors — GPLv2, with this port’s compatibility changes.
  • AdPlug and ScummVM contributors — Westwood ADL interpreter, retained GPLv2-or-later and LGPLv2.1-or-later notices.
  • Nuked OPL3, Nuke.YKT — LGPLv2.1-or-later.
  • SDL2 and Emscripten contributors — zlib and MIT/NCSA licenses.
  • Hyllian — MIT-licensed xBR pixel-art shader.

Download the matching engine source, adapters, build scripts and evidence. Owners supply their own original game data to rebuild. The source archive includes full component notices and the selected SDL2 source archive.
